item.title: Vince Staples Addresses Theory That ‘Cry Baby’ Artwork Represents Donald Trump: ‘I See a Lot of Conversation’
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Welcome to "Trending on Billboard". Today, we're talking about Vince Staples' latest album, "Cry Baby". The Long Beach rapper has been making waves with the album's unique cover art, which features a blonde-haired white baby crying while wearing an American flag diaper.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: Staples recently sat down with Apple Music to explain the meaning behind the cover. He revealed that the baby isn't meant to represent President Donald Trump, but rather the listener themselves. Staples said, "That is you, the listener, that is you as a baby. That is all of us." He went on to explain that the cover represents the socio-political systems we adopt and complain about, and how we feed into them.
[Music transitions]
Host: "Cry Baby" was released on June 5th and has sparked a lot of conversation around its artwork and politically charged subject matter. Staples has also been open about his frustrations with the country and the music industry. During a performance at the El Rey Theatre in LA, he expressed his fatigue with doing press and the pressure to conform to traditional hip-hop sounds.
[Clip of Vince Staples speaking plays]
Vince Staples: "You know, they told me, 'You can't make this, you gotta do straight hip-hop, it's gonna translate better with your audience.' Whatever the f—k that means."
[Music transitions back]
Host: Staples' album has been making waves with its genre-bending sound, and it's clear that he's not afraid to push boundaries. We'll be keeping an eye on "Cry Baby" and Vince Staples' future projects. Thanks for tuning in to "Trending on Billboard".
[Outro music fades in]
